title: Closing the Triple Equivalence: the Converse Commutant Edge
content: The header fixes the three classical conditions on a single matrix M over a field K (Hoffman & Kunze §7.5, Roman §10.4): (i) M has a cyclic vector; (ii) minpoly M = charpoly M (nonderogatory); (iii) the centralizer C(M) = {N : NM = MN} equals the polynomial algebra K[M]. The parent biconditional gives (i)⟺(ii) and the sibling oq-02 gives the forward edge (i)⟹(iii); this file supplies the remaining converse edge (iii)⟹(ii), hence ⟹(i), closing the triangle. The proof is a dimension squeeze combining three facts: dim K[M] = deg(minpoly), dim C(M) ≥ n, and deg(minpoly) ≤ n. The Status note isolates the one classical input not yet in Mathlib — the Frobenius bound dim C(M) ≥ n — as a single disclosed axiom and confirms everything else is axiom-free.

title: dim K[M] = deg(minpoly) via the First Isomorphism Theorem
content: finrank_adjoin_eq_natDegree_minpoly computes dim_K K[M] = deg(minpoly K M). Because the matrix algebra is noncommutative, the PowerBasis API for Algebra.adjoin does not apply directly; instead K[M] is realized as the range of aeval M : K[X] →ₐ[K] Matrix (Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval), whose kernel is the ideal (minpoly K M) (minpoly.ker_aeval_eq_span_minpoly). The first isomorphism theorem (Ideal.quotientKerEquivRange) gives K[M] ≅ K[X]/(minpoly), and finrank_quotient_span_eq_natDegree reads off its K-dimension as deg(minpoly).

title: The Frobenius Bound dim C(M) ≥ n — the Single Isolated Axiom
content: finrank_centralizer_ge is the file's only assumption: the centralizer of any n×n matrix has K-dimension at least n. This is a classical theorem (Frobenius, 1878). Its standard proof views Kⁿ as a K[X]-module via M, identifies C(M) with the ring of K[X]-module endomorphisms End_{K[X]}(Kⁿ), decomposes Kⁿ into invariant factors K[X]/(f₁) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ K[X]/(f_k) (rational canonical form), and notes the block-diagonal scalar multiplications already span a subspace of dimension Σ deg fᵢ = n (in fact dim C(M) = Σ_{i,j} deg gcd(fᵢ,fⱼ), equal to n iff nonderogatory). Mathlib v4.26.0 has the primary-decomposition structure theorem (Module.equiv_directSum_of_isTorsion) and the Module.AEval' K[X]-module structure, but neither the C(M) ≅ End_{K[X]}(Kⁿ) bridge nor the invariant-factor packaging — several hundred lines of infrastructure — so the bound is recorded as one transparently-disclosed axiom.
mathContext: $\dim_K C(M) = \sum_{i,j} \deg\gcd(f_i,f_j) \ge \sum_i \deg f_i = n$, with equality iff $M$ is nonderogatory.

title: deg(minpoly) ≤ n from Cayley–Hamilton
content: natDegree_minpoly_le bounds deg(minpoly M) ≤ n. The minimal polynomial divides the characteristic polynomial (minpoly.dvd applied to Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly — Cayley–Hamilton), and the characteristic polynomial is monic of degree n (Matrix.charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim), so Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd gives the bound. This is the upper half of the squeeze that meets the Frobenius lower bound.

title: The Squeeze and the Capstone: (iii)⟹(ii)⟹(i)
content: centralizer_eq_adjoin_implies_nonderogatory assembles the three facts. From C(M) = K[M] it gets dim C(M) = dim K[M] = deg(minpoly) (rewriting with the hypothesis and finrank_adjoin_eq_natDegree_minpoly), then the Frobenius bound gives n ≤ deg(minpoly) and Cayley–Hamilton gives deg(minpoly) ≤ n. With deg(charpoly) = n this forces deg(charpoly) ≤ deg(minpoly); since minpoly ∣ charpoly and both are monic, Polynomial.eq_of_monic_of_dvd_of_natDegree_le yields minpoly = charpoly. The capstone centralizer_eq_adjoin_implies_cyclic feeds this into the parent biconditional nonderogatory_iff_has_cyclic_vector to produce an actual cyclic vector — the converse edge that closes the triple equivalence cyclic ⟺ minpoly = charpoly ⟺ centralizer = K[M].
mathContext: $n \le \deg(\mathrm{minpoly}) \le n$ forces equality; monic $p \mid q$ with $\deg q \le \deg p \Rightarrow p = q$, so $\mathrm{minpoly} = \mathrm{charpoly}$.
